analysis.investment_thesis: Lloyds Enterprises fails both Magic Formula screens catastrophically: Earnings Yield of ~1.1% (EBIT ₹118 Cr / EV ~₹10,262 Cr) and ROCE of just 5.97% — both far below my minimum thresholds of 12% and 20% respectively. This is a high-priced, low-quality conglomerate with no durable earning power from operations.
key_strengths: Revenue growth is real: ₹1 Cr (2021) → ₹1,488 Cr (2025), 30.9% CAGR shows the business is being assembled
Low leverage: Debt/Equity 0.16, though debt surged from ₹70 Cr to ₹671 Cr in one year
Promoter holding at 62.72% provides alignment, at least on paper
key_risks: Other Income dominates profits: 2022 Net Profit ₹154 Cr on Operating Income of ₹4 Cr; 2024 Net Profit ₹175 Cr with ₹135 Cr Other Income — real operating earnings are a fraction of reported profits
Conglomerate incoherence: steel trading + real estate + engineering + pizza outlets (1441 Pizzeria) = no moat, no focus, no pricing power
Debt exploded from ₹125 Cr to ₹671 Cr in a single year (2024→2025) while OCF remains erratic; capital deployment is opaque
red_flags: Name changed from 'Shree Global Tradefin Limited' in Sept 2023 — classic shell/promoter restructuring vehicle
Revenue was ₹1 Cr in 2020 and 2021; this is not an operating business revival but a new entity assembled around a shell
EV/EBITDA of 78.44x and EV/EBIT of ~87x for a steel trader with 6% operating margins is indefensible
Net profit in 2022 (₹154 Cr) came almost entirely from ₹159 Cr Other Income — likely asset sales or financial gains, not operations
Total assets ballooned from ₹314 Cr to ₹5,582 Cr in 5 years — funded heavily by equity issuances (reserves ₹198 Cr → ₹3,170 Cr), diluting shareholders
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula analysis is decisive here: Earnings Yield of ~1.1% (EBIT ₹118 Cr against EV of ~₹10,262 Cr) ranks this stock near the bottom of any screener. ROCE of 5.97% means the business destroys value relative to its cost of capital. The EV/EBITDA of 78.44x is pricing in a transformation that hasn't materialized operationally. For reference, my formula demands >12% earnings yield AND >20% ROIC simultaneously — Lloyds misses both by an order of magnitude.

The deeper issue is earnings quality. Strip out "Other Income" (₹83 Cr in FY25, ₹135 Cr in FY24, ₹159 Cr in FY22) and the operating business barely earns anything. This is a promoter-assembled conglomerate — formerly a dormant shell — now trading at ₹9,684 Cr market cap on ₹118 Cr of EBIT from steel trading, real estate, and pizza. Free cash flow has been near zero or negative for most of the last 5 years. Borrowings jumping 5x in one year while CWIP rose to ₹132 Cr signals capital is being deployed aggressively with no demonstrated return history. Magic Formula investors should avoid completely.
